llmResponse.agendaChanges: No formal agenda changes were proposed or adopted. Section 7 (Bond Program Action Items), Section 8 (School/Community Reports), Section 10 (Discussion Items), Section 14 (Correspondence) had no items taken up. The three SPSA approvals under Section 9 were handled sequentially with presentations and votes embedded within Section 9. Consent items under Section 11 were approved as a bundle. No items were pulled.

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: Kindergarten teacher at Hoover spoke about the negative impacts of large class sizes and the high number of students with IEPs and behavioral needs in her classroom of 27.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: Retired Redwood City kindergarten teacher urged the board to address large kindergarten class sizes and the slow timeline for identifying and assessing students with special needs.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: RCTA membership chair announced that the Redwood City Teachers Association unanimously voted to endorse the upcoming parcel tax, praising its equitable structure and projected $12.2 million annual revenue.

publicComments.name: Thomas Rogerson
publicComments.summary: Henry Ford and North Star parent argued that teacher quality matters most but urged the board to consider class size impacts on equity and teacher retention, especially in heterogeneous classrooms.

publicComments.name: Araceli Flores Mendoza
publicComments.summary: Second-year education specialist at Hoover described the challenges of high caseloads and minimal aide support, requesting that the board provide two aides for Hoover resource teachers next year.

publicComments.name: Anne Briljafa
publicComments.summary: Longtime TK teacher presented data on the complex needs of incoming kindergartners and urged the board to keep kindergarten class sizes as small as possible.

publicComments.name: Lisbeth Estrada
publicComments.summary: Hoover parent (speaking in Spanish, with interpretation) thanked the board for recent investments and requested extended TK hours, expansion of TK at Hoover, and classroom aides for kindergarten and first grade.

publicComments.name: Heather McCormick
publicComments.summary: Henry Ford parent of a third grader with a class of 32 described physical and instructional constraints of large classrooms and expressed concern about students leaving the school.

publicComments.name: Augustine Espino
publicComments.summary: Kennedy parent expressed concern about large class sizes and urged community support for the parcel tax, emphasizing the need to demonstrate results for the Latino community.

publicComments.name: Pam Barash
publicComments.summary: 36-year kindergarten teacher at Henry Ford urged the board to address class sizes, warning against becoming the only San Mateo County district with 30-to-1 kindergarten ratios in her final year before retirement.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez-Monet
publicComments.summary: Hoover parent since 2017 and frequent classroom volunteer advocated for reducing class sizes and requested a second Spanish kindergarten class at Hoover.

publicComments.name: Patricia Renderos
publicComments.summary: Hoover TK parent (speaking in Spanish, with interpretation) expressed excitement about positive TK outcomes, said she spreads the word for TK enrollment, and thanked the board for listening.

publicComments.name: Sophia Santos
publicComments.summary: First-year first grade teacher at Hoover spoke about feeling overwhelmed with 27 students and urged the board to reduce class sizes to better meet all students' needs.

publicComments.name: Jackie Moore
publicComments.summary: Special education teacher and Hoover parent of twins advocated for smaller class sizes, paraeducators in every TK–2 classroom, aides for each RLC teacher, and hard caps on SLC caseloads.

publicComments.name: Rajanesh Patarath
publicComments.summary: Marine Corps veteran and Hoover kindergarten parent praised Ms. Herrera's teaching and asked the board to consider the impact of increasing class sizes on students' ability to receive individualized attention.

publicComments.name: Brenna Gear
publicComments.summary: RCTA President asked the board to officially endorse the Prop 55 extension and previewed upcoming presentations on class size, salary, and safety during the current negotiation cycle.

publicComments.name: Maria (CSEA rep)
publicComments.summary: Classified union representative raised concerns about inequitable salary increases for classified employees compared to teachers and administrators, arguing that percentage-based raises leave lower-paid workers further behind.
